name: The Shrouded Isles of Albion
summary: Overview of Avalon's isles beyond the sea: the seven isles from the Isle of Glass to Inishail, each with its own file, and the dungeons beneath them.

facts.text: Albion's Shrouded Isles are Morgana's and the drakoran's war on Avalon, with Arawn's Inconnu fighting for Albion; Morgana raised the undead remains of Roman soldiers for her army.
Three ring-shaped fortresses on an earthen border at the Isle of Glass hold Albion's side; Morgan's influence shows even there, in headless undead, corpse lights and ghosts.

Region 51 holds seven zones: Isle of Glass (51), Avalon Isle (52), Dales of Devwy (53), Caldey (54), Gwyddneau (55), Aldland (56) and Inishail Island (57); each has its own lore file. Avalon City, Caer Sidi, Krondon and the Crystal Cave are dungeons of their own regions.
Welsh legend, not game canon: Gwyddno Garanhir ruled a drowned kingdom, Cantre'r Gwaelod; that the zone name echoes him is to verify.

The isles' named bosses now live in their zone files: Amphiptere, Durval and Vortanos (Caldey); Qan'ris Duros, Ris'nir Cruss and Valnir Mordeth (Dales of Devwy); Coliath (Gwyddneau); Sarcondina and the Spirit of Lord Emthoro (Inishail Island).

story:
Beyond the sea from the king's hills lie the isles of Avalon, which the colleges held for longer than Camelot has stood, and which Albion has mostly lost. Morgana came over the water with the drakoran and the dead, the colleges burned, and the isles fell one after another, until Albion held only the southernmost and threw up a wall across it.

Read from the wall outward, the isles run like this. The Isle of Glass is the last firm ground, Caer Gothwaite and its harbour, the three ring-forts on the earth wall. North of it Avalon Isle keeps the colleges' orchards and the burnt city on its lid of glass, and Wearyall's tree. West of Avalon, Aldland, the hall-folk's old land, keeps Krondon's door under its hill and Albion's safe fort. Beyond Avalon to the north the Dales of Devwy were the colleges' farms, where the dead households still keep house and a drakoran wears a dead master's name. Caldey in the far west was Avalon's burying isle, and stood up when the witch called; the turning gaol of Caer Sidi stands on the water off its strand. Gwyddneau, the heights of a drowned country, is the one isle Albion never held, because the lammia of Clifton hold it. And Inishail, the smallest and last, is a dead lord's ground.

Each isle has its own story now, told in its own place. What they share is the war: drakoran on the high ground, Morgana's dead in the old graves, the Inconnu walking between them on errands for their lord, and Albion's companies crossing the water from Gothwaite Harbor to go down into the dungeons the war left behind. They come for the dungeons. They stay, often longer than they meant to, for the war.
legend: The Shrouded Isles are Albion's expansion zones, levels 1 to 65, reached by the ship from Camelot Hills to Gothwaite Harbor. Start on the Isle of Glass, then Avalon Isle and Aldland, then the Dales of Devwy, Caldey, Gwyddneau and Inishail for the 50s and 60s. Each isle has its own nameds; check the isle's own lore. Avalon City is under Avalon Isle, Krondon's door is on Aldland, Caer Sidi is off Caldey's western strand, the Crystal Cave is reached from Avalon. Learn the trick of a named before you pull.

loremaster.intro: The isles of Avalon, which Albion has mostly lost. Ask of each isle: the [isle of glass], [avalon isle], [aldland], the [dales of devwy], [caldey], [gwyddneau] or [inishail]; or of the dungeons beneath them, [avalon city], [krondon], [caer sidi] and the [crystal cave].

topics.isle of glass: The last firm ground, Albion's foothold: Caer Gothwaite and its harbour, the earth wall and its three ring-forts.
topics.avalon isle: The colleges' orchards, Wearyall's tree, and the burnt city on its lid of glass; [avalon city] lies under it.
topics.aldland: The hall-folk's old land, west of Avalon: [krondon]'s door under the hill, the Kulaclan orcs, and Caer Diogel, the safe fort.
topics.dales of devwy: The colleges' farms, north of Avalon: Fort Gwyntell, the ghost households, the hall of making and the drakoran camp.
topics.caldey: Avalon's burying isle in the far west, which stood up when Morgana called; Little Haven, and [caer sidi] off its strand.
topics.gwyddneau: The heights of a drowned country, the one isle Albion never held: the lammia town of Clifton and the lich on the height.
topics.inishail: The isle of rest, smallest and last: a dead lord's ground, the orcs who ran, and Sarcondina's marsh.
topics.avalon city: The colleges' city, burnt, under Avalon Isle, where the drakoran lords hold court.
topics.krondon: The hall under the hill on [aldland], held by the thrawn ogres and their queen.
topics.caer sidi: Arawn's turning gaol, standing on the water off [caldey]'s western strand.
topics.crystal cave: The cave under Avalon where Xanxicar sleeps on the colleges' warm ground.

book.title: Letters from the Isle of Glass
pages: We hold the three ring-forts on the earth wall and look across at what was Avalon. By day the drakoran patrol the border, and they are soldiers, not beasts, with sergeants and surgeons and a proper watch. By night it is worse, because by night the dead come up to the wall. They march in step. Our Inconnu say they are Romans, legionaries of the old province who were buried in the isles three hundred years ago, and that the witch has given them new orders.

Each isle has its named terror, and the garrison trades stories of them the way soldiers trade dice. The serpent of Caldey that sheds its teeth. The lord's ghost on Inishail who cannot be hurt by anyone who will not set foot on his ground. The keeper of prisoners who is not there after dark. The thing in Gwyddneau that guards something, though nobody can say what. We have a wager on what it is. Nobody has collected.
